posts.title: A message from Fr. Ward
posts.author: Fr. Justin Ward
posts.preview: As we begin this special Year of Saint Francis, I write to you with gratitude and hope. Pope Leo's gift to us this special year offers us a beautiful opportunity to renew our faith…
posts.body:
Dear Brothers and Sisters in Christ,

As we begin this special Year of Saint Francis, I write to you with gratitude and hope. Pope Leo's gift to us this special year offers us a beautiful opportunity to renew our faith, strengthen our parish family, and reflect more deeply on the Gospel through the example of Saint Francis, whose life continues to inspire Christians throughout the world.

Saint Francis embraced a life centered completely on Christ. He chose simplicity over status, service over self-interest, and love over power. His radical trust in God and his joyful spirit remind us that holiness is not reserved for a few, but is a calling given to each one of us. In every generation, the Church needs witnesses who live the Gospel with authenticity and courage. In our own time, we are invited to rediscover that same spirit.

During this Year of Saint Francis, my prayer is that we can be intentionally focused on three themes that marked his life: deeper prayer, generous charity, and grateful stewardship of God's creation.

First, we are called to deepen our life of prayer. Saint Francis encountered Christ personally and allowed that encounter to transform him. Prayer was not merely a duty for him; it was a relationship of love. I encourage every parishioner and family to renew your commitment to daily prayer. Attend Mass faithfully. Spend time in Eucharistic Adoration. Pray the Rosary. Read Sacred Scripture. Even a few quiet moments each day with the Lord can renew our hearts and strengthen our faith.

Second, we are invited to grow in charity and service. Saint Francis saw Christ in the poor, the sick, and the forgotten. He did not turn away from suffering; he embraced it with compassion. As a parish, we will expand opportunities for outreach and service in the months ahead. We are blessed with so many outreach opportunities at St. Mark, but I also know that there may still be more opportunities to establish. I encourage all of you to participate actively — whether by volunteering your time, supporting parish ministries, visiting the homebound, or assisting those in need within our community. When we serve one another, we serve Christ Himself.

Third, we reflect on gratitude for God's creation as a reflection of God's graciousness to us. Saint Francis praised God for the sun, the moon, the earth, and all living things. He recognized creation as a gift entrusted to our care. This year, let us become more mindful stewards of the blessings God has given us — our community, our parish, our families, and our resources. Gratitude leads to responsibility, and responsibility leads to faithful action.

This year is not only about programs or events, though we will certainly have many opportunities that I encourage you to avail yourselves of. But also recall that it is about personal conversion. It is about asking ourselves: Where is God calling me to grow? Where do I need to simplify my life? How can I bring peace into my home, my workplace, and my community? The spirit of Saint Francis challenges us to let go of whatever prevents us from loving God and neighbor more fully.

As your pastor, please know that I am deeply grateful for your faith, generosity, and commitment to our parish. Our community is blessed with many gifts — dedicated volunteers, faithful families, generous supporters, and those who quietly serve behind the scenes. Together, we form the Body of Christ in this place. Together, we can make this Year of Saint Francis a time of renewal and grace.

Saint Mark the Evangelist, pray for us!

Fr. Justin Ward

posts.heading: Parish News
posts.title: The New Saint Mark Children's Choir
posts.author: DeLee Benton
posts.preview: My name is DeLee Michiko Benton, and I am excited to serve as the director of the Children's Choir at Saint Mark the Evangelist…
posts.body:
My name is DeLee Michiko Benton, and I am excited to serve as the director of the Children's Choir at Saint Mark the Evangelist. I have been involved in music for many years as a singer, teacher, choir director, and performer, and I believe music is an essential part of worship, adoration, and parish community life. Singing gives us a meaningful way to express our faith, bring people together, and share our God-given gifts. I hold a Master of Music from Samford and a Bachelor of Music Education from Montevallo. In addition to directing the Children's Choir, I sing with the Saint Mark's Choir, serve as the Executive Director of Birmingham Opera Project, and perform and teach throughout the Birmingham community.

Beginning Wednesday, September 16th, the Saint Mark Children's Choir will meet weekly in Saint Mark's Chapel at 6:30 pm. This opportunity is for students in 2nd–5th grade, and the choir will typically sing once a month as a prelude to the 10am mass during the school year. Rehearsals will take place in a welcoming, faith-filled environment where children can learn, sing, and build community together. No previous choir experience is required. Children do not need to read music or consider themselves soloists. They simply need a willing heart, a joyful spirit, and a desire to learn!

Music benefits children in every area of their development, extending far beyond the rehearsal room. Singing strengthens listening, memory, concentration, coordination, language development, and emotional expression. Learning songs requires children to listen carefully, remember patterns, follow directions, and use their voices and bodies with awareness — skills that support classroom learning, communication, focus, and problem-solving. Performing in a supportive environment builds courage and self-confidence, while working through challenges develops perseverance and resilience.

Participating in a choir teaches children the value of teamwork and shared responsibility. They learn to listen to one another, contribute their individual parts, follow a director, practice patience, and work toward a common goal. Because every voice matters, children discover that a successful choir is created not by one voice alone, but by a community of singers who support and encourage one another. As they grow in their ability to listen, cooperate, and empathize, they develop qualities that enrich their friendships, families, schools, and communities.

For children of faith, music offers a meaningful way to grow spiritually. Through sacred song, prayer, Scripture, and participation in the liturgy, children encounter the Church's teachings in memorable and personal ways. They learn that their voices and abilities are gifts they can offer in service to God and others, while singing together nurtures reverence, gratitude, compassion, and a deeper sense of belonging to the Body of Christ. Music can reach us spiritually in ways words alone sometimes cannot: a hymn may help us pray when we do not know what to say, comfort us in sorrow, awaken gratitude, or open our hearts to God's presence. When we sing together, we are not merely learning notes and rhythms; we are participating in a form of prayer that can shape us inwardly and draw us closer to God and one another.

Music tugging at our heartstrings is an experience many of us can speak to and have encountered before. Even now, I cannot sing "Amazing Grace" without crying! Its words, melody, and memories reach a place in my heart that ordinary conversation cannot always reach. These experiences remind us that music is more than something we perform — it can minister to us, help us encounter grace, and express what words cannot. My favorite Scripture verse, Matthew 6:34, reminds us to remain present, trust in God, and take each day as it comes.

Growing up, music provided me with a safe and welcoming place to express myself, build confidence, and connect with others. I hope to offer that same environment to the children of Saint Mark's: a place where every child feels welcomed, valued, and encouraged to discover the joy of music and faith, growing not only as young musicians but also in confidence, friendship, and their sense of belonging within the Church. I look forward to welcoming our young singers and supporting them as they grow in music, faith, confidence, and joyful service.

Families who would like more information are invited to contact the parish office, email me at delee@stmarkrc.org, or speak with me directly. I am excited to build this ministry alongside the music staff, children, and families of Saint Mark the Evangelist as we make music together in service to our parish and our faith.

Sincerely in Christ,
DeLee Michiko Benton
